audit.why: FAV at 4/10 with a 52.42% win rate over 1013 games is consistent, and the mirror agrees the lane is Tryndamere's to lose. Difficulty is about the clock, not the trades.
audit.corrected: Left as is; breakdown.mid retargeted from an empty 'track her R' instruction to her heal and auto-reset timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every side in the full layer disagreed with its own why and with the packet chart: rows 1-4 were marked Tryndamere while the whys called them even, and row 5 was marked Skill while its why says level 6 favours you.
audit.why: The packet chart is Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Tryndamere and the content whys already match it. Level 6 is the real swing: Divine Judgment is 160 seconds at rank 1, so baiting it once leaves her defenceless for several waves.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to the packet chart as one atomic group, ratings adjusted, and the four full-layer whys rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: No ability interaction was stated anywhere — the page repeated 'track Divine Judgment' with no numbers, and Mocking Shout appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160/120/80, so at 6 it is a once-per-three-waves resource, not something to fight around each trade. Starfire Spellblade is an auto reset on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 whose wind-up is the tell. Celestial Blessing heals on a flat 15s. Mocking Shout cuts AD in an 850 radius but slows only enemies with their backs turned, so a Kayle retreating while facing you is not slowed.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, report[5], dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why and spikes[1].

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Kayle contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave. She is melee with no kill threat, but Radiant Blast reaches 900 — do not stand in the sword line.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Kayle's Divine Judgment is down.
edits.after: Neither of you has an ultimate yet. Starfire Spellblade is an 8s auto reset — the wind-up is your cue to step out.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kayle must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but she only wants to farm to 6. Deny the CS instead of chasing a kill you cannot finish yet.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Divine Judgment's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Celestial Blessing heals her every 15 seconds, so buy Executioner's Calling before you commit to long trades and shove her off the wave.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kayle's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage flips the all-in while it runs, and Divine Judgment is 160 seconds at rank 1 — bait the invulnerability once and she is defenceless for three waves.

edits.before: Level 2 stays skill as she pokes and farms without kill pressure.
edits.after: Level 2 stays skill: Starfire Spellblade is an 8s auto reset.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay skill as she scrapes toward her level-6 ranged form.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay skill as Celestial Blessing heals the chip off every 15s.

edits.before: Late game you stay favoured in lane provided you've denied her the farm to scale.
edits.after: Two items in you still win the duel, but only if you denied her the farm to scale.

edits.before: - Kayle Divine Judgment: matchup-defining — Her get-out at 6. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Divine Judgment: 160s at rank 1 — bait it once and she owns nothing for three waves. - Starfire Spellblade: 8s auto reset, the wind-up is the tell. - Celestial Blessing: heals every 15s. - Undying Rage: kill windows only.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Divine Judgment: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade around her 15s heal and her 8s auto reset: commit once both are spent. Retreat facing her — Mocking Shout only slows a back that is turned.

edits.before: Track Kayle's Divine Judgment (Invuln): Her get-out at 6. Bait it. When it is down — Crit her down.
edits.after: Divine Judgment is 160s at rank 1 — bait it, then kill her on the next wave. Mocking Shout slows only turned backs.

edits.before: Her get-out at 6. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 160 seconds at rank 1 — force it out early and the lane is yours.

edits.before: That is Kayle's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: That is Kayle's whole win condition — deny the CS and she never reaches it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Her range and Nashor's out-scale you; take the fight while she is melee.

edits.before: Your level-6 spike is the whole game: Kayle's R Divine Judgment gives her a few seconds of invulnerability, but if you E in, chunk her, and Undying Rage through her ult's damage window, she has no escape to actually get away once her R immunity ends.
edits.after: Your level-6 spike is the whole game: Divine Judgment is 160 seconds at rank 1, so bait it once and the next three waves are free. E in, chunk her, Undying Rage through the holy rain, and she has no escape at all once the invulnerability ends.

notes: The packet's suspectName on wants.you[2] ('Divine Judgment's') is a false positive — the name matches the kit exactly; the mirror reached the same conclusion. Every full-layer side on this page disagreed with its own why before this edit, which is the pattern the two-layer check exists to catch. The page still says 'his win condition' / 'starve him' about Kayle in breakdown.feeding, breakdown.carry, report[12] and dontsFull; I fixed the ones I was already rewriting but the rest are pronoun-only changes with no room in the length band.
